entries.meaning: To go to stores looking for things to buy. ---
examples: We usually shop on Saturday mornings.
They shopped for a used car all weekend.
I hate shopping for clothes.
entries.contrast: Double the p: shopped, shopping. You shop for what you are looking for.

entries.meaning: To have enough money for something. ---
examples: We can't afford a bigger apartment right now.
I could have afforded the trip if I hadn't bought the bike.
He works two jobs and still barely affords the rent.
entries.русский: позволять себе, быть в состоянии купить
entries.contrast: Almost always with can, can't, could or be able to: I can't afford it, not I don't afford it.

entries.meaning: To argue back and forth about a price until both sides agree. ---
examples: At the market you're expected to haggle.
He haggled over the price for an hour.
They spent the morning haggling with the dealer.
entries.contrast: You haggle over a price with a seller.

entries.meaning: To discuss terms with someone until you reach a price both sides accept. ---
examples: Tourists rarely bargain, so they pay more.
The union bargained for higher wages.
We're still bargaining over the price of the truck.
entries.contrast: You bargain with a seller for or over something.

entries.meaning: To decide what something will cost. ---
examples: They price everything a dollar under the competition.
The house was priced too high and sat for a year.
We're still pricing the new models.
entries.contrast: Drop the e before -ing: pricing, not priceing.

entries.meaning: Discount has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Stores discount winter coats in February.
They discounted the sofa by thirty percent.
Everything on this rack is discounted.
Don't discount the possibility that she was right all along.
Investigators discounted the witness's story after checking the timeline.
You shouldn't be discounting his experience just because he is young.

senses.head: To lower the price of something
examples: Stores discount winter coats in February.
They discounted the sofa by thirty percent.
Everything on this rack is discounted.

senses.head: To treat something as unimportant or unlikely to be true
body: (сбрасывать со счетов, не принимать в расчёт)
examples: Don't discount the possibility that she was right all along.
Investigators discounted the witness's story after checking the timeline.
You shouldn't be discounting his experience just because he is young.

entries.русский: делать скидку, уценивать; сбрасывать со счетов, не принимать в расчёт
entries.contrast: As a verb you also hear dis-KOWNT; the noun (a discount) is always DIS-kownt.

entries.meaning: Raise has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Landlords raise the rent almost every year.
They raised forty thousand dollars for the clinic.
Gas prices have been raised twice this month.
She raised the issue at the last meeting.
Nobody wanted to raise the question of money.
Several parents have raised concerns about the new schedule.

senses.head: To make a price or an amount higher, or to collect money for a purpose
examples: Landlords raise the rent almost every year.
They raised forty thousand dollars for the clinic.
Gas prices have been raised twice this month.

senses.head: To bring up a subject, a question, or an objection so that people will deal with it
examples: She raised the issue at the last meeting.
Nobody wanted to raise the question of money.
Several parents have raised concerns about the new schedule.

entries.русский: повышать (цены); собирать (деньги); поднимать, поднять (вопрос); выражать (сомнение, возражение)
entries.contrast: Raise always takes an object (raise prices); the verb with no object is the irregular rise (prices rise).

entries.meaning: To make a price, a rate or an amount smaller. ---
examples: If they lower the price, I'll buy it.
The bank lowered our interest rate.
They're lowering fees to win customers back.

entries.meaning: To sell something to whoever offers the most money. ---
examples: They auction the unclaimed bags twice a year.
The painting was auctioned for two million dollars.
He's auctioning his whole record collection online.

entries.meaning: Export has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They export almost half of what they grow.
The company exported ten thousand units last year.
Most of the coffee is exported to Europe.
You can export the table as a CSV file.
I exported my contacts to a spreadsheet.
The chart has already been exported to PDF.

senses.head: To sell and send goods to another country
examples: They export almost half of what they grow.
The company exported ten thousand units last year.
Most of the coffee is exported to Europe.

senses.head: To save data out of a program in a form that another program can open
examples: You can export the table as a CSV file.
I exported my contacts to a spreadsheet.
The chart has already been exported to PDF.

entries.русский: экспортировать, вывозить; экспортировать, выгружать (данные из программы)
entries.contrast: The verb is ik-SPORT, the noun EK-sport — the stress moves.

entries.meaning: Import has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We import most of our fruit in winter.
The parts were imported from Korea.
They stopped importing steel after the tariff.
You can import your contacts from a spreadsheet.
I imported the photos into the editor last night.
The app is importing your calendar now.

senses.head: To buy goods from another country and bring them in
examples: We import most of our fruit in winter.
The parts were imported from Korea.
They stopped importing steel after the tariff.

senses.head: To bring a file or data into a program from somewhere else
examples: You can import your contacts from a spreadsheet.
I imported the photos into the editor last night.
The app is importing your calendar now.

entries.русский: импортировать, ввозить; импортировать, загружать (данные в программу)
entries.contrast: The verb is im-PORT, the noun IM-port.

entries.meaning: To keep goods in a store so that customers can buy them. ---
examples: We don't stock that brand anymore.
They stocked the shelves before opening.
The store is well stocked for the holidays.
entries.русский: держать в продаже, иметь в ассортименте

entries.meaning: To fill a store or a shelf again after the goods have been sold. ---
examples: They restock every Tuesday morning.
The shelves were restocked overnight.
We're restocking your size next week.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (restock the shelves), intransitive (we restock on Mondays)

entries.meaning: To put something up for sale, usually with a price. ---
examples: I'm going to list the bike online tonight.
She listed the house for four hundred thousand.
The item has been listed for a month with no offers.

entries.meaning: To pay for goods or work with other goods or work instead of money. ---
examples: Some neighbors still barter instead of paying cash.
He bartered a week of carpentry for a used piano.
They were bartering eggs for firewood.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (barter eggs for wood), intransitive (they still barter)

entries.meaning: To exchange a check for money. ---
examples: You can cash a check at any branch.
She cashed her paycheck on Friday.
He's at the bank cashing the check now.
entries.contrast: Add -es after -sh: cashes.
entries.phrasal verbs: cash in · cash in on · cash out

entries.meaning: To send a business a written bill for goods or work. ---
examples: We invoice clients every two weeks.
She invoiced them for forty hours.
The parts were invoiced separately.

entries.meaning: Overcharge has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Restaurants near the airport overcharge for everything.
The garage overcharged us by a hundred dollars.
I think we're being overcharged.
Don't overcharge the battery or it will swell.
He overcharged the cells and ruined the pack.
The batteries had been overcharged overnight.

senses.head: To make someone pay more than the correct price
examples: Restaurants near the airport overcharge for everything.
The garage overcharged us by a hundred dollars.
I think we're being overcharged.

senses.head: To put too much electricity into a battery
examples: Don't overcharge the battery or it will swell.
He overcharged the cells and ruined the pack.
The batteries had been overcharged overnight.

entries.русский: брать лишнее, завышать цену; перезаряжать (аккумулятор), перезарядить
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (they overcharged me), intransitive (that shop overcharges)

entries.meaning: Tax has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The state taxes restaurant meals.
They taxed the sale at eight percent.
Cigarettes are taxed heavily here.
These meetings tax my patience.
The long climb taxed her strength.
Caring for a newborn alone is taxing.

senses.head: To make people pay money to the government on goods, income or property
examples: The state taxes restaurant meals.
They taxed the sale at eight percent.
Cigarettes are taxed heavily here.

senses.head: To make heavy demands on someone's strength, time, or patience
examples: These meetings tax my patience.
The long climb taxed her strength.
Caring for a newborn alone is taxing.

entries.contrast: Add -es after -x: taxes.

entries.meaning: To make someone pay money as a punishment. ---
examples: They fine you fifty dollars for parking there.
He was fined two hundred for paying late.
The city has been fining landlords who ignore the rule.
entries.contrast: Same spelling as the adjective fine (good), but here it means money paid as a punishment.

entries.meaning: To examine something professionally and state its value. ---
examples: A specialist will appraise the painting.
The house was appraised at less than the asking price.
He appraised the jewelry in ten minutes.
entries.contrast: Not the same word as apprise (uh-PRYZE), which means to inform someone.

entries.meaning: Audit has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The IRS can audit returns up to three years old.
Their books were audited last spring.
An outside firm is auditing the accounts.
You can audit the course for free if you don't need the credit.
She audited two graduate seminars before she applied.
I'm auditing a Spanish class this semester.

senses.head: To check someone's financial records officially
examples: The IRS can audit returns up to three years old.
Their books were audited last spring.
An outside firm is auditing the accounts.

senses.head: To attend a college course without taking the exams or earning credit
examples: You can audit the course for free if you don't need the credit.
She audited two graduate seminars before she applied.
I'm auditing a Spanish class this semester.

entries.русский: проводить аудит, проверять отчётность; слушать курс вольнослушателем, посещать без зачёта

entries.meaning: To make money coming in equal money going out in an account. ---
examples: She balances the register every night.
I finally balanced my checkbook.
The budget has to be balanced by June.

entries.meaning: To spend less money than before. ---
examples: When the rent went up, we had to economize.
They economized by cooking at home every night.
She's been economizing since she lost her job.
entries.contrast: American spelling -ize; British writes economise.

entries.meaning: Conserve has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Small shops have to conserve cash in the winter.
They conserved fuel by driving less.
The company is conserving money by not hiring.
The trust works to conserve wetlands along the coast.
The town conserved its old courthouse instead of tearing it down.
Several rare species are being conserved in the park.

senses.head: To use something carefully so that it lasts longer
examples: Small shops have to conserve cash in the winter.
They conserved fuel by driving less.
The company is conserving money by not hiring.

senses.head: To protect a natural place, a species, or an old building from harm or loss
examples: The trust works to conserve wetlands along the coast.
The town conserved its old courthouse instead of tearing it down.
Several rare species are being conserved in the park.

entries.русский: беречь, экономно расходовать; сохранять, охранять (природу, памятники), сберечь

entries.meaning: To spend money on something useless. ---
examples: Don't waste money on the extended warranty.
We wasted three hundred dollars on a printer we never used.
He's wasting his savings on lottery tickets.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like waist (the middle of the body).

entries.meaning: To spend a lot of money on something you don't really need, as a treat. ---
examples: Once a year we splurge on a nice hotel.
She splurged on a leather jacket.
They're splurging a little for their anniversary.
entries.contrast: You splurge on something.

entries.meaning: To waste a large amount of money foolishly. ---
examples: He squanders every paycheck the week he gets it.
They squandered the inheritance in two years.
She had squandered a fortune before anyone noticed.

entries.meaning: To make money out of a deal or a situation. ---
examples: Resellers profit from every shortage.
He profited nicely when the stock split.
Nobody is profiting at these prices.
entries.contrast: You profit from something, and the verb sounds exactly like prophet.

entries.meaning: Diversify has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Advisers always tell you to diversify.
She diversified her savings after the crash.
The firm is diversifying into groceries.
Small stores have to diversify to survive.
The farm diversified into cheese and weekend tourism.
The company has been diversifying away from print for a decade.

senses.head: To put money into several different things so that one loss cannot ruin you
examples: Advisers always tell you to diversify.
She diversified her savings after the crash.
The firm is diversifying into groceries.

senses.head: For a business to start selling new kinds of products or move into new activities
examples: Small stores have to diversify to survive.
The farm diversified into cheese and weekend tourism.
The company has been diversifying away from print for a decade.

entries.русский: диверсифицировать, распределять вложения; расширять ассортимент, осваивать новые направления
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (diversify your savings), intransitive (investors should diversify)
entries.contrast: -y after a consonant becomes -ies and -ied: diversifies, diversified.

entries.meaning: Possess has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Almost nobody possesses enough cash to buy a house outright.
She possessed very little when she arrived.
Everything possessed by the company was sold to pay the debt.
What possessed you to tell her that?
In the movie a demon possesses the youngest child.
He tore through the house like a man possessed.

senses.head: To have something, especially as property
examples: Almost nobody possesses enough cash to buy a house outright.
She possessed very little when she arrived.
Everything possessed by the company was sold to pay the debt.

senses.head: To take complete control of someone's mind or behavior, as a spirit or a strange impulse is said to do
body: (овладевать (кем-л.), овладеть; вселяться (о духе); находить (что на тебя нашло))
examples: What possessed you to tell her that?
In the movie a demon possesses the youngest child.
He tore through the house like a man possessed.

entries.русский: обладать, владеть; овладевать (кем-л.), овладеть; вселяться (о духе); находить (что на тебя нашло)
entries.contrast: The ss in the middle sounds like a z: puh-ZESS.

entries.meaning: To borrow money using your house or land as security. ---
examples: They had to mortgage the farm to keep it running.
The house was mortgaged twice.
He's mortgaging his future to pay for school.
entries.contrast: The t is silent: MOR-gij.

entries.meaning: Redeem has 2 distinct senses.
examples: You can redeem the coupon at any branch.
She redeemed her points for a flight.
The gift card has already been redeemed.
One good scene can't redeem a bad movie.
He redeemed himself with a touchdown in the last minute.
The film is redeemed by its final twenty minutes.

senses.head: To exchange a coupon, a voucher or points for goods or money
examples: You can redeem the coupon at any branch.
She redeemed her points for a flight.
The gift card has already been redeemed.

senses.head: To make up for a mistake or a fault and win back people's good opinion
examples: One good scene can't redeem a bad movie.
He redeemed himself with a touchdown in the last minute.
The film is redeemed by its final twenty minutes.

entries.русский: погашать; отоваривать (купон); искупать, искупить (вину); реабилитировать себя, исправить впечатление

entries.meaning: To pay part of the cost of something so that others pay less. ---
examples: The state subsidizes bus fares for students.
Housing was subsidized for low-income families.
Taxpayers are subsidizing the whole project.
entries.contrast: American spelling -ize; British writes subsidise.

entries.meaning: To give official permission to sell something, or to let a company use your name or design for money. ---
examples: The state licenses every dealer.
The design was licensed to a toy company.
They're licensing the name to three manufacturers.
entries.contrast: American English spells the noun and the verb the same, license; British spells the noun licence.

entries.meaning: Convert has 3 distinct senses.
examples: The app converts dollars to euros instantly.
We converted the last of our cash at the airport.
Prices are converted at yesterday's rate.
They converted the garage into a bedroom.
Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity.
The old factory is being converted into apartments.
He converted to Judaism before the wedding.
Missionaries tried to convert the whole village.
She was converted by a book she read in college.

senses.head: To change money from one currency into another
examples: The app converts dollars to euros instantly.
We converted the last of our cash at the airport.
Prices are converted at yesterday's rate.

senses.head: To change something into a different form or a different use
examples: They converted the garage into a bedroom.
Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity.
The old factory is being converted into apartments.

senses.head: To change your religion, or to make someone else change theirs
body: (обращать в веру; переходить в другую веру)
examples: He converted to Judaism before the wedding.
Missionaries tried to convert the whole village.
She was converted by a book she read in college.

entries.русский: конвертировать, обменивать (валюту); превращать, переделывать, преобразовать; обращать в веру; переходить в другую веру
entries.contrast: The verb is kuhn-VURT, the noun KAHN-vurt.

entries.meaning: Swipe has 4 distinct senses.
examples: Swipe your card and enter the PIN.
She swiped the card twice by mistake.
He was still swiping when the machine froze.
Swipe left to delete the message.
She swiped through her photos the whole train ride.
He kept swiping at the screen with wet hands.
Someone swiped my umbrella from the hallway.
Don't leave your phone where a kid can swipe it.
Half the candy had been swiped before the party started.
The cat swiped at my hand.
A bear can swipe hard enough to break bone.
He was swiping at flies with a dish towel.

senses.head: To pass a bank card through a machine to pay
examples: Swipe your card and enter the PIN.
She swiped the card twice by mistake.
He was still swiping when the machine froze.

senses.head: To slide a finger across a touchscreen
examples: Swipe left to delete the message.
She swiped through her photos the whole train ride.
He kept swiping at the screen with wet hands.

senses.head: To steal something small, in informal speech
examples: Someone swiped my umbrella from the hallway.
Don't leave your phone where a kid can swipe it.
Half the candy had been swiped before the party started.

senses.head: To hit out at something with a quick sweeping movement
examples: The cat swiped at my hand.
A bear can swipe hard enough to break bone.
He was swiping at flies with a dish towel.

entries.русский: проводить картой, прокатывать карту; проводить пальцем по экрану, смахивать, листать; стащить, стянуть, украсть (по мелочи); махнуть (лапой, рукой), ударить наотмашь

entries.meaning: To officially charge a tax, a fee or a fine. ---
examples: The city levies a small tax on hotel rooms.
They levied an extra charge on late payments.
A fine was levied against the company.
entries.contrast: -y after a consonant becomes -ies and -ied: levies, levied.

entries.meaning: To replace a loan with a new one, usually at a lower rate. ---
examples: Rates dropped, so a lot of people are trying to refinance.
They refinanced the house at a lower rate.
The loan has been refinanced twice.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (refinance the mortgage), intransitive (we refinanced last year)

entries.meaning: To leave something valuable at a shop in exchange for money you can repay to get it back. ---
examples: He'll pawn the guitar if rent is short.
She pawned her ring to cover the bill.
The watch has been pawned and bought back twice.

entries.meaning: To make an amount twice as large, or to become twice as large.
examples: Shipping costs can double around the holidays.
The rent doubled in six years.
They're doubling the size of the store.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (double the price), intransitive (the rent doubled)
entries.phrasal verbs: double back · double down · double over · double up
